reasons: Section 19 supports the compliant classification: 19.1 gives the professional/workmanlike services warranty, 19.2 gives a ninety-day (plus full subscription term for Hosted Services) conformance-to-documentation warranty, 19.3 covers malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law, and 19.4 supplies re-performance/repair/replacement escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid — meeting the preferred position on all material terms.

The disclaimer in 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly states no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty; no 'AS IS' walk-away language is present.
No redline and no counterparty comment is the correct output for a compliant finding, and the rationale accurately cites the clause text and the acceptance-stage mechanics in 6.2.

The failed deterministic check is a false negative from phrasing: the period is spelled out as 'For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later,' which satisfies the ≥90-day benchmark.
